title: Trump: William Barr's father hires Jeffrey Epstein at Dalton School
description_short: Trump: William Barr's father hires Jeffrey Epstein at Dalton School
description_medium: Jeffrey Epstein began teaching mathematics and physics at New York's Dalton School in September 1974. Donald Barr, father of later Attorney General William Barr, was the school's headmaster until that summer. The linked reporting says it is unclear whether Barr took part in hiring Epstein; students later recalled concerning behavior, but the sources do not show what administrators knew when he was hired.
description_long: Jeffrey Epstein began teaching mathematics and physics at Dalton School in September 1974, after Donald Barr, the school's headmaster and father of future Attorney General William Barr, had announced his departure. The New York Times later reported that students remembered Epstein as an unusual teacher who pushed school norms and crossed boundaries in interactions with girls. Some students said they raised concerns with an administrator, but the available account does not date those reports to the hiring process. It also does not establish that Donald Barr personally hired Epstein or that Dalton officials knew of specific misconduct when he joined the faculty. The record connects two biographical facts—Barr's leadership at Dalton and Epstein's appointment—but the timing and decision-makers behind the hiring remain unclear. Later recollections of Epstein's conduct should not be treated as proof that school administrators knew of abuse before or at the time he was hired.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: William Barr's father hires Jeffrey Epstein at Dalton School
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: William Barr's father hires Jeffrey Epstein at Dalton School

notes: Source reading: The Times dates Epstein's start at Dalton to September 1974 and says students later recalled concerning conduct. The reporting does not establish that Donald Barr hired him; Barr had announced he would leave at the end of the 1973–74 school year. Student concerns are described, but their timing relative to hiring and what administrators knew then are not established.

title: Trump: CNP List: Over 1,000 Past & Present Members of the Council for National Policy
description_short: Trump: CNP List: Over 1,000 Past & Present Members of the Council for National Policy
description_medium: The Council for National Policy was founded in 1981 as a private gathering place for conservative organizers, donors and activists. A linked 1981 New York Times report described the group's early meetings; a separate later archive publishes a list claiming more than 1,000 past and present members. Neither source documents Donald Trump's membership at the time of the council's founding.
description_long: The Council for National Policy was organized in 1981 as a private forum for conservative leaders, activists and donors. A New York Times report from that year described the emerging group and its effort to coordinate conservative policy work. The linked Trump Timeline page, updated decades later, publishes a list labeled as more than 1,000 past and present CNP members. That list is a separate compilation, and the page's political characterizations should not be treated as a neutral account of the council's influence. The available sources do not provide the full underlying membership records, a documented account of the group's later activities, or evidence that Donald Trump belonged to it in 1981. A later address or association would not establish membership at the time of its founding. The council's existence and early purpose are documented, but the scope of the list and the Trump connection need clearer sourcing before the entry can link them as one event.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: CNP List: Over 1,000 Past & Present Members of the Council for National Policy
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: CNP List: Over 1,000 Past & Present Members of the Council for National Policy

notes: Source reading: The 1981 Times article describes the council's early organization; the Trump Timeline page later publishes a list claiming over 1,000 past and present members. The linked sources do not provide full membership records or establish Trump's membership or involvement at the 1981 founding.

title: Trump asks FBI for protection in Atlantic City, help with investigations
description_short: Trump asks FBI for protection in Atlantic City, help with investigations
description_medium: In April 1981, Donald Trump spoke with FBI agents about his plan to build a casino in Atlantic City and his concerns about organized crime and the licensing process. A later FBI memorandum records discussions with an informant connected to the property and a proposal for undercover assistance. The records show a planned October meeting, but do not establish that it occurred or that the FBI opened an investigation.
description_long: FBI records reproduced in the linked account describe an April 1981 meeting with Donald Trump as he considered entering Atlantic City's casino business. Trump discussed concerns that organized-crime allegations could affect licensing and his family name, and offered to cooperate with the bureau. An FBI memorandum also describes Daniel Sullivan, an informant with connections to the criminal underworld who had a business interest in property Trump wanted for a casino. Agents drafted a proposal for an undercover operation and anticipated discussing it with Trump at a meeting scheduled for Oct. 1, 1981. The documents establish that the FBI considered a plan and that Trump met with agents; they do not show whether the scheduled meeting took place, whether the proposal was approved, or whether the bureau launched an investigation based on it. The record therefore documents contact and a proposed cooperation arrangement, not a completed operation or a finding that Trump was an FBI informant.

preserved_fields.title: Trump asks FBI for protection in Atlantic City, help with investigations
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump asks FBI for protection in Atlantic City, help with investigations

notes: Source reading: The TrumpFile page reproduces FBI interview and planning documents describing Trump's April 1981 meeting, an undercover proposal, and a planned Oct. 1 follow-up. It does not establish that the follow-up occurred, that the proposal was approved or implemented, or that an investigation was opened.

title: Trump: Epstein's Early Empire: Maxwell, Mogilevich, Mossad, and the CIA
description_short: Trump: Epstein's Early Empire: Maxwell, Mogilevich, Mossad, and the CIA
description_medium: The linked archive dates Jeffrey Epstein's launch of Intercontinental Assets Group to Aug. 18, 1981, after he left Bear Stearns. It describes the firm as a consulting business that claimed to help recover money for clients. The same page advances claims about organized crime and intelligence links, but does not supply corporate records or official findings that substantiate those characterizations.
description_long: The linked Trump Timeline page dates Jeffrey Epstein's creation of Intercontinental Assets Group Inc. to Aug. 18, 1981, after his departure from Bear Stearns. It describes the company as a consulting firm that purported to help clients recover money from allegedly fraudulent brokers and lawyers. The page then makes broader claims about transnational crime and intelligence agencies, but the material provided does not establish the firm's registration, clients or documented business activity. Nor does it substantiate the claims that Epstein's company operated for organized crime or an intelligence service. Assertions about Robert Maxwell, Semion Mogilevich, Mossad or the CIA require records beyond the archive's narrative and allegations attributed to others. The source supplies a date and a description of how the business presented itself; it does not support treating its most serious claims as established findings. The relationship between the firm and the wider Epstein story remains unverified in the cited material.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Epstein's Early Empire: Maxwell, Mogilevich, Mossad, and the CIA
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Epstein's Early Empire: Maxwell, Mogilevich, Mossad, and the CIA

notes: Source reading: The page gives Aug. 18, 1981, as IAG's launch and describes its claimed consulting activity. It does not provide registration records, client documentation or official findings substantiating the organized-crime or intelligence allegations; those claims remain unverified here.

title: Trump: Carl Icahn destroys industry giants, helps debilitate the Midwest
description_short: Trump: Carl Icahn destroys industry giants, helps debilitate the Midwest
description_medium: In May 1985, Trans World Airlines asked federal regulators to block Carl Icahn's hostile bid, arguing that he lacked airline-management experience and might sell assets for a quick profit. TWA warned that routes and facilities, including those in St. Louis, could be at risk. The linked article records the dispute at that stage, not the later takeover terms or its economic effects.
description_long: In May 1985, Trans World Airlines petitioned the Department of Transportation to block Carl Icahn's hostile takeover attempt. The airline argued that Icahn lacked experience operating an air carrier and might buy shares for a quick profit rather than maintain the business. TWA warned that a takeover could lead to asset sales or cuts to routes and facilities, including operations in St. Louis. Those statements were the company's claims during a contested bid, not a record of what ultimately happened to each facility or employee. The linked Washington Post report establishes that TWA opposed Icahn's effort and explains its concerns; it does not document the final acquisition terms, later staffing reductions, or measured effects on St. Louis. Other accounts of union concessions and employee stock arrangements would be needed to assess the takeover's impact. The record can describe the dispute and its stated risks, but should not present those predicted harms as completed consequences without later evidence.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Carl Icahn destroys industry giants, helps debilitate the Midwest
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Carl Icahn destroys industry giants, helps debilitate the Midwest

notes: Source reading: The May 1985 Washington Post report records TWA's request that DOT block Icahn's bid and its allegations about management experience and potential asset/route cuts. It is contemporaneous with the contested offer and does not establish final terms, employee outcomes or regional economic effects.

title: Trump: Former Trump executive releases book detailing racism & stupidity
description_short: Trump: Former Trump executive releases book detailing racism & stupidity
description_medium: John R. O'Donnell, a former president of Trump Plaza Hotel and Casino, published Trumped! in 1991. A TrumpFile page reproduces excerpts from a New York Times review dated July 14, including O'Donnell's attributed account of remarks about Black accountants. The linked material does not establish the book's exact release date or provide the entire review and underlying passages.
description_long: John R. O'Donnell, formerly president of Trump Plaza Hotel and Casino, published Trumped! The Inside Story of the Real Donald Trump in 1991. A Trump Timeline page says the book reached stores around the time of its May 1, 1991 entry and reproduces excerpts from a New York Times review published July 14. The excerpt reports O'Donnell's account of Donald Trump making racist remarks about Black accountants and includes a quotation attributed to Trump by O'Donnell. The review also describes O'Donnell's claims about Trump's handling of publicity after a 1989 helicopter crash and casino spending. These are allegations in a former executive's book as summarized by the reviewer, not independently established facts in the excerpt. The linked archive provides selected passages rather than the full review or the underlying book pages. It also does not give a precise publication-day record. A complete review or the book itself is needed to verify the passages and place them in context.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Former Trump executive releases book detailing racism & stupidity
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Former Trump executive releases book detailing racism & stupidity

notes: Source reading: The archive identifies John R. O'Donnell, the 1991 book, and reproduces selected passages from the New York Times review dated July 14, 1991. The page says the book hit stores but does not establish the exact publication date or provide the full review/book text; the quoted claims remain attributed to O'Donnell.

title: Donald Trump taps Vanity Fair to help him launch his comeback
description_short: Donald Trump taps Vanity Fair to help him launch his comeback
description_medium: In December 1993, Donald Trump asked Vanity Fair for a profile as he sought to revive his public image. The magazine assigned writer Edward Klein to spend several days with him during the month, and published the feature in March 1994. The source documents an editorial profile and access arrangement, not a promotional partnership or promise of favorable coverage.
description_long: In December 1993, Donald Trump asked Vanity Fair to feature him during his effort to rebuild his public image after a series of business setbacks. The magazine assigned writer Edward Klein to spend several days with Trump over the course of the month; the resulting profile appeared in March 1994. The linked archive quotes Klein describing Trump's view that the press could “build you back up” after cutting you down, and frames the access as part of a comeback effort tied to a planned public offering. The source documents a profile Trump requested and the reporter's access arrangement. It does not show that Vanity Fair agreed to promote Trump or that the magazine guaranteed a favorable story; the profile was editorial coverage produced by the publication. The distinction matters because the claim that Trump “tapped” the magazine can describe his request and the access he offered, but not a business or promotional partnership. The archived account identifies the reporter, approximate reporting period and publication window, while the full Vanity Fair profile would provide the complete treatment.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump taps Vanity Fair to help him launch his comeback
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump taps Vanity Fair to help him launch his comeback

notes: Source reading: The linked archive says Trump requested a feature, Edward Klein spent several days with him during December 1993, and the profile appeared in March 1994. It documents access for a journalistic profile, not a promotional/business arrangement.

title: Trump: FBI reports on Semion Mogilevich's transnational organized crime operation
description_short: Trump: FBI reports on Semion Mogilevich's transnational organized crime operation
description_medium: A 1996 FBI report described Semion Mogilevich's organization as a transnational criminal group of about 250 people and outlined its operations and U.S. business links. The report said Mogilevich had associates in the Russian government, while qualifying gaps in what investigators could trace. The cited report does not connect Mogilevich or the organization to Donald Trump.
description_long: An FBI report prepared for law-enforcement use in 1996 described the Semion Mogilevich Organization as a transnational criminal group with about 250 members. It summarized investigations by a multinational working group and discussed alleged activities, associated businesses, finances and contacts in several countries. The report noted that Mogilevich had associates in the Russian government, but that statement does not establish that the government was controlled by organized crime or that every alleged link was proven. The report also included qualifications about the limits of available information and what investigators could directly trace. The linked material provides no connection between Mogilevich's organization and Donald Trump. The archive's placement of the FBI report in a Trump timeline does not establish such a relationship. This record can describe the report's scope and its allegations, but a sourced Trump connection would be needed to justify presenting it as an event about him.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: FBI reports on Semion Mogilevich's transnational organized crime operation
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: FBI reports on Semion Mogilevich's transnational organized crime operation

notes: Source reading: The reproduced 1996 FBI report identifies an approximately 250-member organization and discusses alleged Russian-government associates with investigative qualifications. It does not link Mogilevich or his organization to Trump; the timeline placement alone is not evidence of a connection.
